 The block was given with an in-plane technique using a 22 G needle, and Group A received 25 ml 0.5%
levobupivacaine with 8 mg dexamethasone as an adjuvant. In contrast, Group B received 25 ml 0.5%
levobupivacaine with 50 mcg dexmedetomidine and 1.5 ml sterile water as an adjuvant.
 Patients were evaluated for the onset time of sensory and motor block and the duration of sensory and
motor block.
 Patients were also evaluated for the time taken for the first dose of rescue analgesia and the requirement of
the total dose of rescue analgesia
 Patients were assessed for postoperative visual analogue scores for both groups at 2, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 24
hours post-surgery.
RESULTS:
 Age and gender were comparable and statistically insignificant.
 The onset time of sensory and motor blockade was significantly faster in Group A than in Group B.
 The duration of action was significantly longer in Group B than in Group A.
 The time taken for the first rescue analgesic is significantly longer in Group B than in Group A.
 The total dose of analgesic given was significantly lower in Group B than in Group A.
 VAS scores were significantly better in Group B than in Group A.
CONCLUSION:
In conclusion, with all the above findings, which are statistically significant, dexmedetomidine has better action as
analgesia than dexamethasone when used as an adjuvant to levobupivacaine for ISBPB in patients undergoing
shoulder surgeries.

Title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DISEASE DIAGNOSIS: POTENTIAL AND LIMITATIONS IN CLINICAL PRACTICE

Description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming medical diagnostics, offering fundamentally new approaches to clinical data analysis. This article, based on an analysis of current scientific publications, examines the potential and limitations of implementing AI systems in clinical practice. Advances in medical imaging, disease prognosis, and clinical decision support are analyzed, as well as critical challenges related to the methodological quality of studies, model interpretability, integration into clinical workflows, and ethical aspects. Particular attention is paid to the challenge of transitioning from demonstrating technical effectiveness to ensuring clinical significance and reproducibility of results. A conclusion is drawn regarding the need for a research paradigm shift: from comparative "AI versus physician" trials to the development of standardized methodological approaches and the creation of explainable, clinically oriented systems.

Title: Theoretical Framework of Agentic Pharmacy

Description: Agentic Pharmacy is proposed as an interdisciplinary field integrating pharmaceutical sciences, artificial intelligence (AI), multi-agent systems, systems engineering, digital health, data science, and healthcare management. Unlike existing concepts such as AI Pharmacy or Digital Pharmacy, which primarily focus on technological tools, Agentic Pharmacy introduces a comprehensive framework centred on intelligent AI agents capable of autonomous reasoning, collaborative decision-making, adaptive learning, and coordinated pharmaceutical operations while maintaining human oversight.

Title: Agroforesterie : élevage résilient et cycles des nutriments

Description: Cette affiche a pour objectif de susciter des échanges entre paysans et éleveurs lors d’ateliers consacrés à l’agroforesterie, en mettant l’accent sur l’intégration des arbres, des arbustes et du bétail dans les systèmes agricoles sahéliens.

L’affiche décrit les synergies et les cycles de nutriments suivants :

Les arbres et arbustes fournissent des feuilles et des fruits nutritifs, ainsi que de l’ombre, ce qui améliore la santé du bétail et la qualité des produits d’origine animale. En retour, le bétail produit du fumier riche en nutriments qui améliore la fertilité et la santé des sols, ce qui renforce la rétention d’eau et augmente les rendements des cultures. En protégeant et en favorisant la croissance et la régénération des arbres et arbustes, les agriculteurs peuvent s’assurer un approvisionnement continu en fourrage de haute qualité, créant ainsi un système agricole plus résilient, plus productif et plus durable.

Cette affiche s’appuie sur les résultats du projet Sustain Sahel. Nous remercions sincèrement tous les agriculteurs, producteurs et scientifiques dont les connaissances et les contributions ont rendu ce travail possible.

Title: Dorudon serratus Gibbes 1845

Description: Dorudon serratus Gibbes, 1845
Dorudon serratus Gibbes, 1845: 254.
Basilosaurus serratus Gibbes, 1847: 255.
Zeuglodon brachyspondylus minor Müller, 1851: 240 (in part).
Zeuglodon serratum – Abel 1914: 204.
TYPE MATERIAL. — Holotype . United States • 1 specimen (fragments of the skull and mandible including deciduous dentition, and a partial atlas of a juvenile individual, see Kellogg 1936); South Carolina, Berkeley County, Mazyck Plantation; [33°30’0”N, 80°5’59”W]; Harleyville Formation, Priabonian, Late Eocene; MCZ [MCZ 8763]. TYPE LOCALITY. — Mazyck Plantation, Berkeley County, South Carolina, United States (Uhen 2013a). TYPE HORIZON AND AGE. — Harleyville Formation, Priabonian, Late Eocene.
REFERRED SPECIMENS. — USNM 16638, USNM 16639, FMNH PM-459, USNM MMNS VP 130.
DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS. — Dorudon serratus can be separated from Dorudon atrox by the following features: the lack of an anterior process on the frontals in adult specimens (this study); the presence of an extra mesial accessory denticle on dP2, three in total (Uhen 2004); a weaker lingual projection on the dP3 and dP4 (Andrews’s posterointernal buttress; Uhen 2004) the presence of large vertebroarterial foramina on the mid-cervical vertebrae (diameter greater than the upper bounding bony rim; this study).
DISCUSSION
The type of D. serratus consists of teeth, skull fragments and some vertebrae from a juvenile individual (Kellogg 1936; Uhen 2013a). The species has mostly remained restricted to the type species (Kellogg 1936), but additional specimens of D. serratus were recognized by Uhen (2013a), including MMAS A and MMNS VP 130. These reassignments were based on dental morphology (Uhen pers. comm.). Dental differences between D. serratus and Zy. kochii have emerged as the main diagnostic feature separating the two taxa in existing literature. The diagnostic feature for D. serratus being the presence of a smaller, non-crenulated cingulum on the upper premolars. These premolars are not present in USNM 16638, USNM 16639, and FMNH PM-459, meaning this feature cannot be used to diagnose these specimens. Instead, relying on the posterior narial region, USNM 16639 is nearly identical to that of MMNS VP 130, it seems more likely this specimen belongs to D. serratus . FMNH PM-459 possesses neither upper premolars, not a posterior narial region, but does possess a more rounded nuchal crest and double rooted p1 like MMNS VP 130, and USNM 16639. USNM 16638 possesses deciduous dentition, allowing for direct comparison with the holotype of D. serratus . Uhen (2013a) described a more prominent cingulum on the dP2-4 of this specimen as compared to MCZ 8763, however only Kellogg (1936) mentions a slight cinguloid ridge on the labial surface below the distal two denticles of dP 3 in his description of the deciduous dentition of USNM 16638. No mention of any cingulum is given in any of the other described teeth. Suggesting the difference is based only on a slight difference in cingulum on one tooth. Given the number of crenulated cingula differs between USNM 11962, and MSC 3927 (Daly 1999), it seems that this difference can be related to intraspecific variation. More detailed assessments of dental morphology are needed to say for certain what the meaning of these differences is. Diagnostic cranial differences between Zygorhiza kochii and Dorudon serratus are given in Figure 7. The vertebral proportions of basilosaurids are considered highly diagnostic (Uhen 2005; Gingerich 2007; Uhen 2013a; Martínez-Cáceres et al. 2017). Uhen (2004; 2013a) states that Zygorhiza possesses vertebrae slightly smaller and less robust than those of Dorudon spp. When we compared the vertebral lengths of specimens from Chrysocetus healyorum , Dorudon serratus and Zygorhiza kochii we did not find significant differences correlating with skull morphology (Fig. 8). The most major interspecific difference is the small size of the C. healyorum holotype, however this specimen is also a juvenile (Uhen & Gingerich 2001). Thus, it is not clear if this difference is actually taxonomically informative. Instead, the most major variation was found in the posterior thoracic, lumbar, and anterior caudal vertebrae. With this exception, all specimens possess similarly sized cervicals and anterior thoracics, after which a pattern of stepwise increasing variation is seen moving posteriorly across the torso series (viz. Buchholtz 2001: posterior thoracic, lumbar, and anterior caudal vertebrae). AUMP 2368 (associated with the skull MSC 3927), possesses the shortest vertebrae, diverging from the other specimens midway through the thoracic series. USNM 4678 and USNM 12063 only diverge at the posteriormost thoracic vertebrae. The longest lumbars are seen in MMNS VP 130 and USNM 4679.
DESCRIPTION OF SPECIMEN TM 8501
TM 8501 consists of a skull, mandibles, and some associated postcrania including portions of seven vertebrae, three ribs, two sternebrae and a partial basihyal. None of the appendicular skeleton was recovered. Based on the completed dental eruption and fused epiphyses on vertebrae, TM 8501 represents a mature individual. Figure 9 shows the location of elements in-situ (Fig. 9A) and in life (Fig. 9B).
SKULL
The maximum anteroposterior length of the skull is 811 mm, with the rostrum measuring (anterior margin of orbit) 484 mm. The general shape of the rostrum is elongated and narrow (Fig. 10B, D). Anterior of the bony nares, the depth and width increase gradually (Fig. 10A), with the width being greater than the depth. At the level of I2, the rostrum is 50 mm deep and 63 mm wide. This width and depth profiles increase gradually moving posteriorly.The bony nares is located dorsally to P1, with the posterior margin located dorsally to the mesial edge of P2. The bony nares marks a large increase in depth of the rostrum, and the most abrupt of all height changes in the lateral silhouette of the skull. ...

Title: Building a window into the Software Heritage Cathedral

Description: Open-source software is a foundational part of the research ecosystem, yet institutions often lack visibility into the software they produce and use, who maintains it, and how it contributes to their impact. This presentation introduces OSPO-Radar , a Software Heritage project funded by the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, which provides research institutions, OSPOs, funders, and infrastructures with tools to manage, document, and share their open-source work.

OSPO-Radar acts as the missing layer between institutions and the Software Heritage universal source code archive, addressing both the fragmentation of the current landscape and the long-term preservation of research software.

In this short pitch, the current status (a two-year effort), and the collaboration model inviting co-design partners, pilot institutions, advisory members, and open-source contributors. Mutualisation across interoperable ecosystems is positioned as key to the sustainable recognition and preservation of research software.

Title: The Topographic Writing of Women's Lives into the Sacred Landscape of the Argolid

Description: This science communication article explores how ancient Greek societies utilized their physical environment to regulate women’s lives, sexuality, and reproduction . Focusing on the Argolid region, the study applies the anthropological concept of "topographic writing" to demonstrate that the natural landscape served as a legible canvas for social control and collective memory . Rather than relying solely on civil laws, the ancient polis embedded biopolitical regulations—such as marriage and legitimate lineage—into sacred topographies and religious rituals overseen by deities like Aphrodite . Through specific case studies, the research decodes the 'topograms' of the Argolid, including embodied prenuptial hair offerings to Hippolytus in Troezen, the reproductive regulatory node of Aphrodite’s temple in Hermione for both brides and widows, and the ritualized gender subversion of the Hybristika festival in Argos . These sacred spaces and practices functioned as a panoptic tool, transforming strict patriarchal norms into unquestionable divine laws . Ultimately, reading the mnemohistory inscribed in the landscape allows the HIEROTOPOI project to move beyond male-centric historical narratives, successfully recovering the marginalized, lived experiences of ancient women .

This publication is part of the digital outreach and knowledge transfer strategy for the HIEROTOPOI project (10.55776/PAT2141125).

Title: Zwischen Autonomie und didaktischer Anleitung

Description: Abstract

Generative AI has become a routine companion in secondary computing education, yet unguided access to ready-made solutions threatens the very learning processes that project-based learning (PjBL) is designed to foster. This thesis investigates how the degree of didactic guidance built into an AI tutor affects teaching and learning in project-based programming instruction.

Methodology

In a five-week quasi-experimental mixed-methods field study, 49 ninth-grade students at an Austrian technical secondary school completed physical computing projects (using the Raspberry Pi Pico and MicroPython) under one of two conditions:

- A didactically guided, Socratic AI tutor configured to withhold complete solutions (complemented by an AI reflection journal capable of asking probing questions).

- Unguided AI access (accompanied by a traditional worksheet for reflection).

Both conditions were provided on the same GDPR-compliant platform. Three data levels were triangulated:

- Focus groups with teachers and pre-service teachers ( N = 12, evaluative qualitative content analysis, 208 codings).

- 374 logged chat sessions comprising 2,665 prompts (quantitative log analysis and structuring qualitative content analysis).

- A standardized post-test ( N = 40).

Results

Teachers judged AI use strictly by project phase, endorsing only guided scaffolding while insisting that creative ideation remain AI-free and rejecting AI process data as a basis for summative assessment.

The process data reveal that restriction changed how , not whether , students used AI: guided groups interacted more frequently, requested ready-made code significantly less often ( p = .047, r = -.83), engaged in more co-constructive dialogue, and produced a more than threefold higher share of analytical reflection ( p = .030, r = .44).

Experience measures (support quality, cognitive load, perceived learning) did not differ between conditions; however, 38.1% of students with guided access categorically rejected AI tutors as harmful, compared to 5.3% with free access ( p = .021). This dissociation is interpreted as psychological reactance to perceived paternalism rather than as a consequence of a poorer experience.

Conclusion

The findings converge on a model of qualitative dosing: restrict solution generation rather than access, calibrate the restriction to project phase and prior knowledge, and communicate it as a justified pedagogical structure. Practical guidelines for configuring and framing AI tutors in K-12 computing education are derived.

Keywords: Generative AI, Computing Education, Project-Based Learning, AI Tutors, Secondary Education, K-12

Title: The Market for Attention: Platform Architecture, Download Friction, and the Download-to-View Ratio in Cross-Listed Scholarly Papers

Description: This paper examines the download-to-view ratio for 169 scholarly papers held simultaneously on SSRN and Zenodo, using the cross-listed structure as a natural experiment in which the work is held constant and only the platform varies. The central finding is that the same paper exhibits a usage ratio 2.49 times higher on Zenodo than on SSRN (paired median ratio; 95% bootstrap CI 2.23 to 2.70; geometric-mean ratio 2.60; Hodges-Lehmann 2.58). Zenodo's ratio exceeds SSRN's for 108 of 111 papers in a conservative single-file subset (paired Wilcoxon p = 1.1 x 10^-19; rank-biserial 0.99; paired Cohen's d_z = 1.81 on the log-ratio), and the direction holds across natural sciences, engineering, and social sciences. Because the work is held constant, no property of the work can explain the difference. The paper argues that the effect is not primarily behavioral but a case of measurement noninvariance: SSRN and Zenodo do not define a "view" or a "download" equivalently, so their usage ratios are not the same quantity and are not directly comparable. Several non-exclusive mechanisms are consistent with the gap, including asymmetric counting rules (Zenodo counting file previews and direct-link downloads, SSRN filtering anonymous downloads from its counted total), differing download friction, and differing user-intent profiles; the data narrow but do not fully identify their relative contributions. A secondary hypothesis, that the gap would be modulated by title technicality, returns a null (beta = -0.10, p = 0.12), though with a placeholder technicality measure that limits its weight. The download-to-view ratio, treated in the scientometrics literature as a property of the paper, is better understood as a joint product of the paper and the platform's measurement architecture, and is not portable across platforms without explicit adjustment.

Title: Rapid Scan on Early Learner Classroom Observation and Teacher Performance Tool Design and Deployment in Low-Resource Settings

Description: This paper explores the design and deployment of classroom observation tools to support teacher professional development and instructional supervision in low-resource and crisis-affected settings. Drawing on a rapid evidence scan conducted for the Ministry of Education in Yemen, the study reviews international classroom observation frameworks and assesses two observation tools currently used to support general pedagogy and early grade literacy instruction. The review identifies five key principles of effective observation systems: technical quality, pedagogical relevance, standardisation, clarity of purpose, and contextual alignment. Findings suggest that while the Yemeni tools align well with recognised dimensions of effective teaching and literacy instruction, they face challenges related to reliability, scoring consistency, and the provision of actionable feedback for teacher improvement. The paper argues that classroom observation tools are most effective when used as developmental instruments that support coaching and professional growth. It concludes with practical recommendations for strengthening tool design, observer training, and implementation approaches in resource-constrained education systems. An output of the EdTech Hub, https://edtechhub.org/

Available from https://docs.edtechhub.org/lib/ERIPJ48W

Title: Tensiones en la práctica docente. Entre desafíos y posibilidades

Description: Vislumbrar las tensiones por las que viven los profesores es una tarea obligada para los pensadores, político y funcionarios educativos. Al maestro siempre se le ha cargado el peso de la concreción de las reformas educativas; aparentemente se le aplaude y reconoce por su papel trascendental en los cambios educativos, por su loable tarea de educar; sin embargo, poco se habla de mejorar sus salarios, de las muchas exigencias que lleva a cuestas todos los días, de lo peligroso que es trabajar con los niños de ahora, frágiles emocionalmente. El fenómeno de vivir en tensiones nos lleva al análisis de las emociones, de la salud amenazada, del estrés, del desgaste… Y eso es lo que abordan precisamente los capítulos de esta obra, que conforman la primera parte de la obra.

En la segunda se ubican los capítulos que con optimismo plantean posibilidades de salida, lo que llamamos el lado luminoso o quizás grisáceo de la luna, en el que no todo es protervo. Así, con optimismo los autores plantean el trabajo colaborativo como alternativas a las tensiones, el tejer saberes juntamente con la consideración de la otredad, innovando y recreado en la docencia

Title: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Faithfulness An Intervention-Based Analysis of Reasoning-Unit Necessity

Description: CoT faithfulness was tested on a small, simple experiment. Models ( Gemma 4 26B A4B IT , GPT-OSS-20B , and NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra ) were asked to generate answers using CoT on questions from three different datasets ( GSM8K , StrategyQA , and ARC Challenge ), and were also asked to give an importance score to each step they used. Afterwards, each step was removed from the CoT, and the models were asked to answer again using only the question and the remaining steps. This was used to test how the models’ answers changed when any particular step was removed, as well as whether the importance scores they provided were actually meaningful.

Title: AI for Holistic Medicine: Understanding Multi-Organ Interactions in Cancers

Description: Cancer is no longer viewed as a disease confined to a single organ. Modern research shows that tumors influence the immune system, metabolism, hormones, blood vessels, microbiome, and distant organs throughout the body. This broader perspective has encouraged the development of holistic and systems-based medicine, where physicians and researchers attempt to understand cancer as a dynamic network of interactions rather than an isolated mass of abnormal cells. Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a critical tool in this transformation because it can analyze enormous and complex biological datasets that humans alone cannot fully interpret. Traditional oncology often focused on a single tumor site, such as breast, lung, or colon cancer. However, cancer progression depends on communication between multiple organs and biological systems. For example, liver metabolism can influence drug effectiveness, the gut microbiome can affect immune responses, and chronic inflammation in one organ may accelerate tumor growth elsewhere. Metastasis itself is a multi-organ process in which cancer cells travel through the bloodstream and colonize distant tissues. AI-driven holistic medicine aims to map these interconnected pathways and reveal patterns that may improve diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning. One of the most important contributions of AI in holistic cancer medicine is the integration of “multi-omics” data. Multi-omics refers to combining information from genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and epigenomics to create a comprehensive picture of disease biology. Each layer provides different insights into how cancer behaves. Genomics identifies DNA mutations, transcriptomics examines gene activity, proteomics studies proteins, and metabolomics tracks chemical changes in cells and organs. AI algorithms can merge these data sources to identify hidden relationships that may not be visible through conventional statistical methods. Machine learning and deep learning models are especially valuable because cancer datasets are extremely large and multidimensional. AI systems can detect subtle molecular signatures associated with treatment resistance, early metastasis, or organ-specific complications. For example, researchers now use AI to study how tumors interact with the immune system and distant organs during disease progression. These models help predict which patients are likely to respond to immunotherapy, chemotherapy, or targeted drugs. In precision oncology, AI can also personalize treatments by matching therapies to a patient’s unique biological profile. Another emerging area is AI-assisted radiomics, which combines medical imaging with molecular analysis. Advanced AI models can extract thousands of hidden imaging features from CT scans, MRI scans, and PET scans. When combined with multi-omics data, these imaging insights help physicians understand how tumors affect surrounding tissues and distant organs. AI-driven radiomics may allow clinicians to monitor disease spread earlier and evaluate systemic effects without invasive procedures. Holistic medicine also emphasizes the importance of lifestyle, nutrition, and environmental factors in cancer care. AI can analyze longitudinal patient data, including diet, physical activity, wearable sensor data, microbiome composition, and medication history. By integrating these variables, AI systems may identify how external factors contribute to cancer progression or recovery. Researchers believe this approach could support preventive medicine and reduce the side effects of aggressive cancer therapies. Recent advances in systems biology further support the idea of multi-organ AI models. Scientists are developing “digital twin” frameworks that simulate the biological behavior of individual patients across multiple organs and physiological systems. These computational models may eventually predict how cancer evolves over time and how treatments influence the entire body rather than a single tumor. Early research into multi-organ AI endophenotypes has already demonstrated how AI can identify shared disease mechanisms across the brain, heart, eyes, and cancer-related pathways. Despite its promise, AI in holistic cancer medicine still faces challenges. Data privacy, algorithm bias, limited clinical validation, and difficulties integrating hospital systems remain major barriers. Many AI models also function as “black boxes,” making it difficult for physicians to fully understand their reasoning. Nevertheless, ongoing research continues to improve transparency and reliability. In the future, AI may transform oncology from a reactive discipline into a predictive and preventive science. By understanding cancer as a multi-organ and system-wide disease, holistic AI-driven medicine has the potential to improve early detection, personalize treatment, reduce side effects, and enhance patient outcomes. The combination of AI, systems biology, and multi-omics research is therefore shaping a new era of precision and holistic cancer care.

Title: From Teacher-Centred to Student-Partnered: Advancing Inclusive Assessment through Rubric Co-Construction

Description: This chapter explores how co-constructing assessment rubrics can help to foster inclusive, learner-centred assessment practices in higher education. Through a review of recent literature and three institutional case studies, it showcases how co-creating assessment rubrics can support student learning. This was achieved through a unique faculty development initiative at Munster Technological University (MTU). The Re-imagining Assessment and Feedback Together (RAFT2) initiative provides a scaffolded model for transforming practice institutionally. The RAFT initiative operates as a year-long, institutionally supported action research cycle, structured across two semesters: the first focused on problematising assessment in partnership with students, and the second on implementing and evaluating a responsive intervention (O’Mahony, 2026). The selected case studies suggest that rubric co-construction can support assessment literacy, student agency and more inclusive communication of assessment criteria, particularly when students are meaningfully involved in the design process. The chapter argues that co-creation in assessment not only improves assessment clarity but also promotes cultures of collaboration, trust and equity.

Title: Cuidados de Enfermagem Às Mulheres em Situação de Violência Doméstica e Familiar à Luz da Lei Maria da Penha: Revisão Integrativa

Description: A violência doméstica e familiar contra a mulher constitui grave problema de saúde pública e violação dos direitos humanos, com repercussões físicas, psicológicas, sexuais, morais, patrimoniais e sociais. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar os cuidados de enfermagem evidenciados na literatura científica para a assistência às mulheres em situação de violência doméstica e familiar, à luz da Lei Maria da Penha. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, de abordagem qualitativa e caráter descritivo, realizada nas bases SciELO, LILACS, BDENF e BVS, com apoio complementar de normativas oficiais consultadas no Site Oficial do Planalto. Foram incluídos artigos em português, disponíveis na íntegra, publicados entre 2020 e 2026, relacionados aos cuidados de enfermagem às mulheres em situação de violência doméstica e familiar. Os achados foram organizados em cinco categorias temáticas: acolhimento humanizado e escuta qualificada; identificação de sinais físicos, psicológicos, sexuais e sociais da violência; registro e notificação compulsória; encaminhamento à rede intersetorial de proteção; e fragilidades enfrentadas pela Enfermagem nesse cuidado. Conclui-se que a atuação da Enfermagem deve ultrapassar o atendimento pontual às lesões físicas, assumindo uma perspectiva integral, ética, humanizada e articulada à rede de proteção, contribuindo para a segurança, autonomia e dignidade das mulheres.

Title: La Poesía de la Arquitectura – Introducción: Traducción al castellano del artículo de John Ruskin bajo el pseudónimo de Kata Phusin (1837)

Description: Esta publicación presenta la traducción al castellano de la Introducción de The Poetry of Architecture (1837), una serie de artículos tempranos de John Ruskin, publicados originalmente bajo el seudónimo Kata Phusin en The Architectural Magazine . La edición ofrece el texto original en inglés y su traducción al español en formato paralelo, facilitando la consulta, el análisis comparado y la investigación histórica. La traducción se distribuye bajo licencia CC BY 4.0 y contribuye a ampliar el acceso en lengua española a un texto temprano de Ruskin, en el que la arquitectura es concebida como una expresión del sentimiento y del pensamiento humanos, más allá de la mera corrección técnica, y donde se introducen las nociones de «poesía de la arquitectura», «unidad de sentimiento» y carácter nacional como principios fundamentales para comprender la belleza arquitectónica.

Title: ПРИМЕНЕНИЕ ДАТЧИКОВ И СИСТЕМ ДИАГНОСТИКИ В АВТОМОБИЛЯХ

Description: В статье рассматриваются современные датчики и системы диагностики, применяемые в автомобильной промышленности. Анализируются их функции, принципы работы и влияние на безопасность, экономичность и экологичность транспортных средств. Особое внимание уделяется роли электронных систем управления, бортовой диагностики и интеллектуальных технологий мониторинга технического состояния автомобиля. Исследование показывает, что внедрение современных датчиков и диагностических комплексов способствует повышению надежности транспортных средств, снижению эксплуатационных затрат и своевременному выявлению неисправностей.

Title: Ensino aprendizagem na prática: leitura na escola para a construção do saber

Description: O processo da leitura e da compreensão textual na educação básica é fundamental para repensar as práticas pedagógicas que têm sido desenvolvidas e para que com isso se consiga gerir um conhecimento proeficiente. A educação, é um pilar básico da sociedade, e trata-lá com seriedade deveria ser de longe a obrigação de todo governo. Sabendo disso, de acordo com as pesquisas desenvolvidas por Morais (2016) e Perfetti, Landi e Oakhill (2013), o principal objetivo da leitura está na compreensão daquilo que se lê, seja qual for a razão por que se lê, e, além disso, é preciso se ensinar os processos mais eficazes para se chegar à compreensão. Com isso, o foco dessa dissertação é a ampliar o conhecimento a respeito da leitura, mais especificamente, da compreensão em leitura no contexto escolar, a partir da análise da Escola Municipal de Amarra Couro, situada na zona rural do município de Barra/BA. O estudo caracteriza-se como uma revisão bibliográfica e também qualitativa, com aplicação de um questionário de observação, direcionado aos professores e alunos referentes também às técnicas de leitura aplicada aos alunos. Com esse estudo, nota-se o quão importante é o investimento de ações com esse fim, pois é necessario uma maior atenção e capacitação continuada de seus professores. Além disso, é urgente que se estabeleça uma relação de parceria entre universidades e escolas, a fim de que descobertas recentes, fruto de pesquisas acadêmicas, estejam acessíveis para aplicação na educação básica.

Palavras-chave: Leitura eficiente, Projetos de Leitura, Estratégias de Leitura, Processo de ensino e aprendizagem da leitura

Title: Intoxicações Exógenas por Alimentos e Bebidas no Brasil: Análise Epidemiológica de 2020 A 2023

Description: Os casos de intoxicações exógenas por alimentos e bebidas nas diferentes regiões de saúde do Brasil podem se agravar dependendo do acesso aos serviços de saúde e do tipo de agente tóxico envolvido. O presente estudo tem como objetivo avaliar o perfil epidemiológico das intoxicações exógenas por alimentos e bebidas notificadas no Brasil entre 2020 e 2023. Trata-se de um estudo transversal, descritivo e retrospectivo dos casos de intoxicações exógenas por alimentos e bebidas notificadas no Brasil. Os dados foram coletados no segundo semestre de 2024 pelo Departamento de Informática do Sistema Único de Saúde e obtidos a partir do Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação. Foram encontradas 31.182 notificações de intoxicação por alimentos e bebidas em todo o Brasil por intoxicação exógena. A análise dos dados exibiu um aumento no número dessas intoxicações ao longo dos anos estudados, destacando o perfil predominante de homens entre 20 e 59 anos, cor parda, com notificação por confirmação clínica, por exposição aguda e única e com evolução de cura sem sequela. É indispensável implementar políticas de prevenção específicas para enfrentar esse problema crescente, embora o alto número de notificações com informações incompletas ou em branco represente um desafio.

Title: The Geometry of Computation Topological Gaps, Coordinate Inversions, and the Resolution of Complexity Paradigms

Description: The Geometry of Computation

Topological Gaps, Coordinate Inversions, and the Resolution of Complexity Paradigms

Driven by Dean Kulik

July 2026

Introduction: The Dielectric Geometry of Information

Classical computational theory has long been predicated on the temporal execution of sequential logic. From the earliest formalized Turing machines to modern von Neumann architectures, computation is universally modeled as an iterative, chronological evolution of states: . However, a rigorous mathematical and physical analysis reveals that this sequential "forward stream" is merely an artifact of the coordinate system chosen by an external observer. When computation is reframed as a geometric and topological structure, the concepts of time, algorithmic delay, and computational complexity cease to be fundamental physical laws. Instead, they emerge as projections of spatial coupling.

The foundational axiom of this framework requires examining the boundary conditions between two active processes—specifically, a reading process and a writing process. In any computational or physical system, a dielectric gap—a structural delay or separation—is geometrically required only when a reader and a writer are topologically "facing" one another, or when one is nested within the other. Two processes running in parallel without information exchange require no physical or temporal separation; they merely coexist without interaction. But the moment these processes couple—when the write mechanism directly feeds the read mechanism—a dielectric gap becomes structurally mandatory to prevent a degenerate short circuit.

This short circuit is the mathematical equivalent of evaluating in zero time, yielding an infinite, unresolvable loop that computes nothing. In nested systems, where an internal computational model operates inside the external environment it seeks to represent, the dielectric gap is the sole boundary maintaining the distinction between the model and the modeled reality. Without this gap, the internal representation collapses into the external world, losing its capacity to compute, abstract, or predict. Therefore, the "lag" or "latency" observed in classical computation is not fundamentally a temporal constraint. It is a relational constraint. The gap is a geometric necessity of the coupling. If the topological arrangement of the system is altered so that the components no longer face each other, the necessity for the dielectric vanishes, and the computational distance collapses.

This report presents an exhaustive theoretical synthesis that maps the classical "forward stream" of sequential execution against the "side stream" of direct-address computation. By anchoring this analysis in the Bailey-Borwein-Plouffe (BBP) formula for , tridiagonal Jacobi matrices, orthogonal similarity transforms, Geometric Complexity Theory, and the physics of delay-coupled oscillators, this treatise demonstrates that algorithmic complexity—and specifically the versus problem—is an expression of coordinate topology. Hardness in computation does not arise from the sheer volume of a search space, but rather from the topological impossibility of incrementally navigating from a coupled basis to a diagonalized one.

The Physical Topology of the Gap: Dielectrics and Delay Systems

To understand the geometric necessity of the gap in abstract computation, it is necessary to first examine how this gap physically manifests in electromagnetic and dynamical systems. The physical world rigorously enforces the dielectric gap to preserve the integrity of interacting states.

Transmission Lines and Dielectric Propagation

In high-speed printed circuit boards (PCBs) and digital data transmission lines, signals do not propagate instantaneously. The transmission line propagation delay () is the finite duration of time a data signal takes to travel from the source (the writer) to the load (the reader).

This delay is intrinsically tied to the characteristic impedance () of the line, which is defined by the distributed inductance () and capacitance (). The propagation delay per unit length is defined precisely as the square root of the inductance-capacitance product:

The physical separation between the conductive traces is filled with a dielectric material. The dielectric constant (, or relative permittivity) governs the speed at which electromagnetic signals propagate, acting as a frictional medium that slows the signal relative to the speed of light in a vacuum ( m/s).

In this physical architecture, the driver and the receiver face each other across the conductive trace. The dielectric material is the physical instantiation of the geometric gap. Without this gap—if the impedance is severely mismatched, or if the dielectric material is fundamentally inconsistent—the signal suffers massive reflections, parasitic stray capacitance, and data skew.

The mechanical equivalent of this phenomenon is wave propagation along a string with varying mass densities. If an impulse travels along a string with density and hits a boundary connected to a string of density , the behavior is entirely dictated by the impedance matching at the boundary. If (representing a short circuit or an immovable boundary), there is full reflection with the signal inverted. If the impedance is perfectly matched, the wave passes through with no reflection. The dielectric gap is precisely what prevents the read/write pair from degenerating into a chaotic short circuit.

Delay-Coupled Oscillators and Neural Feedback

The geometric requirement for a gap is even more pronounced in dynamical systems with feedback, such as biological neural networks, genetic regulatory circuits, and physical oscillatory rings. ...

Title: Geometric Containment of Nonlinear Instability

Description: This paper formalizes geometric containment of nonlinear instability as the operational regime in which local chaos remains transport-limited relative to a declared coherent region and failure scale on a finite timescale. Local instability, diagnosed by a positive finite-time Lyapunov exponent, is a property of the tangent dynamics along a trajectory. Operational confinement is a property of phase-space geometry. The two are independent: exponential separation of nearby orbits does not by itself imply that an uncertainty envelope will reach the boundary that defines loss of coherence.

Within the Trojan normal-form setting developed in related work, containment is realized by a spectral-gap-protected, near-integrable skeleton. An elliptic–elliptic equilibrium whose linear frequencies satisfy a finite-order non-resonance condition admits a Birkhoff normal form whose truncated part is integrable. Residual invariant tori, cantori, and narrow resonant layers confine chaotic motion to thin stochastic bands whose diameter in the relevant transport coordinate remains much smaller than the distance to the failure boundary. The resulting thinness ratio stays strictly less than one, typically of order 10−2 10^{-2} 1 0 −2 or smaller. Nekhoroshev-type estimates further bound action drift on exponentially long intervals while the gap and remainder hypotheses persist.

Thin chaos is the typical contained state: positive Lyapunov exponents coexist with geometric isolation of the chaotic component. Weak and strong chaos classify the magnitude of the instability rate; thin and thick chaos classify its transport consequence. These axes are independent. Containment is maintained by spectral protection that excludes low-order resonances, by barrier integrity that limits flux, by the continued validity of a two-mode reduction, and by averaging that converts non-resonant coupling into slow residual drift.

Loss of containment occurs through an exhaustive hierarchy of structural exits—separatrix splitting, resonance overlap, spectral-gap collapse, or activation of additional modes—that exhaust the ways the Trojan defining conditions can fail. The passage from thin to thick chaos is therefore a connectivity transition: isolated chaotic layers become linked by non-negligible flux to the failure region. Any claim of operational nonlinear stability must therefore include a transport-sensitive diagnostic; a purely local instability measure is insufficient. The entire construction applies only to systems that admit the Trojan architectural signature and is always relative to an explicitly chosen coherent region, failure scale, and timescale.

Title: Geo3D-AI-CSU/STA-Indexing: STA-Indexing v1.0

Description: Three-dimensional (3D) geothermal numerical simulation is a key technique for resource assessment and development planning, which generates massive volumes of simulation data with multiple spatiotemporal physical attributes, such as temperature, pressure, and Darcy velocity vectors. Efficient retrieval of such 3D simulation database under combined spatial, temporal, and attribute constraints remains a major challenge. To address this challenge, this study proposes a spatio-temporal-attribute unified indexing method, STA-Indexing, on geothermal 3D numerical simulation databases. The method is designed for both 3D scattered points and structured voxels, and it supports three representative attribute types of categorical, scalar, and vector attributes. We use a single rowkey as the unified index to execute complex queries. Its prefix encodes attribute, spatial, and temporal information, while its suffix stores a unique identifier for each record. To support different data structures, the method adopts spatial encoding based on space-filling curves and multilevel grids, and also uses a two-level temporal encoding scheme to improve physical ordering efficiency. Performance experiments are conducted on databases of different scales. The results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms traditional incremental filtering, especially in large-scale scenarios. It achieves lower query latency and higher query efficiency for a variety of multidimensional query tasks. This methodology provides an efficient data retrieval support for geothermal digital platforms and intelligent energy management systems.

Title: Desicision- Making and ESG integration in internationalitation: The Case of BYD Compny Limited

Description: This paper examines how multinational corporations integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria into their long-term growth and production diversification strategies, departing from traditional international business models that prioritized labor arbitrage and logistical optimization. Adopting a qualitative single-case study methodology focused on BYD Company Limited, a prominent global leader in the New Energy Vehicle (NEV) sector, this research evaluates the firm's recent foreign direct investment (FDI) frameworks and cross-border manufacturing relocations across Hungary, Turkey, and Brazil. The empirical findings demonstrate that localizing supply chains and adopting ecologically preferable production models not only mitigates long-term regulatory exposure but also unlocks green financing opportunities through bond markets while accelerating corporate legitimacy in Western global markets. Consequently, this article provides critical empirical evidence regarding the strategic synergy between environmental sustainability and global economic efficiency in modern multinational strategies, offering key insights for executives and policymakers navigating contemporary ecological transitions.

Title: WUR Mass Spectral Library

Description: On this webpage it is possible to download a high-resolution tandem mass spectral library entirely built at Wageningen University and Research (WUR) through the analysis of high-quality standards. The WUR Mass Spectral Library provides high-quality, manually curated data for a large collection of compounds of interest for multiple scientific fields of study.

The WUR Mass Spectral Library is a collaboration between multiple Wageningen Research institutes and Wageningen University chair groups including, Laboratory of Food Chemistry, Environmental Technology and Wageningen Food Safety Research.

This library is a collection of > 1,300 chemicals among which veterinary drugs, contaminants, pesticides, natural toxins, pharmaceuticals, food-derived small molecules and plant compounds (including metabolites). It was built using an ultra -high-pressure liquid chromatography (UHPLC) system coupled to an Orbitrap IQ-X Tribrid, with positive and negative ESI as the ionization interface depending on the chemical. MSn spectra of all compounds were recorded using HCD fragmentation (5-7 collision energy levels). MSn spectra of food-derived small molecules and plant compounds were also recorded using UVPD fragmentation (3 activation times). The library (> 9,000 mass spectra) can be used for:

Expanding compound annotations
Enables exact matches of compounds through high-quality spectral matching (level 2 identification), which can be combined with retention time (RT) information (level 1 identification), ensuring accurate compound identification.

Targeted and Suspect Screening
Easily implemented in your targeted and suspect screening workflows, improving detection capabilities for specific compounds.

Non-Target Screening
Assists in identifying unknown or analogous compounds in non-target screening, by integrating it with machine learning tools to detect novel compounds.

Please see WUR Website link for additional information and to request download access.

Additional information

Besides the complete WUR Mass Spectral Library, the spectra are also separately available based on their main relevant field of study. All libraries are available in both .db and .msp file format. Details on the methodology can be found in the articles mentioned in the citation instructions section, which will be expanded in the future. Please find the description of each library available through this page below:

- WUR mass spectral library pos/neg - Complete collection of spectra of over 1300 chemicals recorded in positive mode and over 475 chemicals recorded in negative mode at multiple collision energies (HCD) and/or multiple activiation times (UVPD) using RP-UHPLC-MS. The WUR mass spectral library contains all spectra mentioned below, with exception of hte polar substances library spectra.

- WFSR food safety mass spectral library pos/neg - Collection of spectra recorded at multiple collision energies (HCD) using RP-UHPLC-MS that are especially relevant for the field of food safety.

- WFSR polar substances mass spectral library pos/neg - Collection of spectra recorded at multiple collision energies (HCD) using flow injection for polar chemicals that are especially relevant for the field of food safety.

- FCH food small molecules mass spectral library pos/neg - Collection of spectra recorded at multiple collision energies (HCD) and multiple activation times (UVPD) using RP-UHPLC-MS for food-related small molecules that are especially relevant for the field of food chemistry. Note that for this library no noise levels were applied to the spectra since low intensity UVPD-fragments might be relevant. All chemicals in this library are either commercially available standards or purified and/or synthesized chemicals verified by NMR analysis.

- ETE organic environmental pollutants mass spectral library pos/neg - Collection of spectra recorded at multiple collision energies (HCD) using RP-UHPLC-MS for organic environmental pollutants that are especially relevant for the field of environmental analysis.

Title: Poisonous Plants Detection Using Deep Learning

Description: Abstract: Identifying poisonous plants in natural environments is often difficult, yet it is important for protecting both human health and animals. Traditional methods mainly depend on human observation, which can be slow and sometimes unreliable, especially when plants look similar. In this work, we created our own dataset consisting of 1,500 leaf images from seven poisonous plant species. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was then trained to classify these plants based on their leaf characteristics. To improve the learning process, the images were preprocessed and augmented. Instead of relying only on accuracy, the model was evaluated using additional measures such as precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix analysis to better understand its performance. The model achieved a validation accuracy of about 87%, showing that deep learning can be useful for this task. This study provides a dataset, a baseline model, and an evaluation approach that can be useful for future research. Further improvements can be made by increasing the dataset size, using advanced models, and developing practical applications for real-world use.

Summary of morphology.
A group of medium-sized (SVL 22.1–30.1 mm), terrestrial or detriticolous Rhombophryne species. All have a rotund habitus, very similar to the R. laevipes species group. They have bright-orange colouration on the posterior side of the limbs in life, and R. ellae and R. quentini sp. nov . have black inguinal ocelli outlined in white (absent in R. kilonjy sp. nov .). Teeth are present on the maxilla, premaxilla, and postchoanal vomer. Clavicles are present. Skin texture is granular.

Title: La animación a la lectura y el hábito lector en estudiantes de octavo año de Educación General Básica, 2026

Description: La presente investigación tuvo como objetivo determinar la correlación entre la animación a la lectura y el hábito lector en los estudiantes de octavo año de Educación General Básica de la Unidad Educativa “Atenas” de la ciudad de Ambato, durante el período académico 2025–2026. El estudio se desarrolló bajo un enfoque cuantitativo, paradigma positivista, alcance correlacional y diseño no experimental de corte transversal. La población estuvo conformada por 52 estudiantes, por lo que se trabajó con una muestra censal. La técnica utilizada fue la encuesta y el instrumento consistió en un cuestionario estructurado con escala tipo Likert de cinco alternativas, validado mediante juicio de expertos y con confiabilidad determinada a través del coeficiente Alfa de Cronbach. Las variables analizadas fueron la animación a la lectura y el hábito lector, considerando las dimensiones afectiva, cognitiva y práctica. El análisis correlacional, realizado mediante el coeficiente de Spearman, identificó una correlación positiva, moderada y estadísticamente significativa entre ambas variables (ρ = 0,5066; p < 0,05). Asimismo, la dimensión práctica presentó la asociación más fuerte y significativa con el hábito lector (ρ = 0,553; p < 0,001), mientras que la dimensión afectiva (ρ = 0,090) y cognitiva (ρ = 0,252) mostraron correlaciones débiles y no significativas (p > 0,05). Se concluye que la aplicación sistemática de estrategias de animación a la lectura favorece el fortalecimiento del hábito lector; sin embargo, su desarrollo también está influenciado por factores personales, familiares y contextuales, siendo la dimensión práctica la de mayor incidencia en la consolidación de este hábito.

Title: La función jurisdiccional en la acción de gobierno: el ejemplo de la política de vivienda

Description: La utilización de las expresiones «judicialización de la política» y «politización de la justicia» resulta insuficiente para representar la actual contribución de los órganos con funciones jurisdiccionales a la acción de gobierno. Los procesos de reubicación de la producción normativa en los ejecutivos, el carácter programático de la legislación estatal y la fragmentación de los centros de producción normativa generan un escenario donde la función jurisdiccional adquiere un creciente protagonismo. El estudio propone la utilización del término «jurisdicción de gobierno» para analizar el impacto de la función jurisdiccional en la configuración de políticas públicas y la determinación de derechos individuales en sistemas de gobierno multinivel. A partir de un estudio jurisprudencial relacionado con la política de vivienda, el análisis muestra cómo la legislación estatal, aun de carácter programático y sin efecto directo, puede operar como canon interpretativo en la delimitación de competencias entre niveles de gobierno y en la revisión de la actividad administrativa, aunque con una recepción heterogénea en función de la materia y el territorio. Además, la jurisdicción de gobierno refleja un debate interno con posiciones divergentes acerca de cómo conciliar el respeto de las competencias autonómicas en el desarrollo de las políticas públicas con el ejercicio de las competencias transversales del Estado.

Description: الأهداف: تسعى هذه المقالة إلى تحليل «الهندسة الديدكتيكية» للظواهر اللغوية في برامج اللغة العربية المقررة في مشروع الإعداديات الرائدة، وذلك بالتركيز على كيفية تحويل القواعد اللغوية من أُطرٍ نظرية جامدة إلى أدوات وظيفيّة تُستعمل لإنجاز أفعال كلام محددة في سياق تواصلي فعلي.

الإشكالية: تتركزُ الإشكالية التي تسعى المقالة إلى الإجابة عنها في رصد الفجوة البيداغوجية والديدكتيكية بين اكتساب القاعدة اللغوية وتملّكها وظيفيا في سياق فعل تواصلي مؤثّر، وبعبارة أخرى: كيف حاولت برامج اللغة العربية في مشروع المدرسة الرائدة ردم الهوّة بين المعرفة الواعية بالقواعد اللغوية وبين الإنتاج الوظيفي لتلك القواعد في سياقات تواصلية محددة؟؛

المنهجية: تعتمد هذه المقالة مقاربة وصفية تحليلية لمسار بناء التعلّمات اللغوية في برامج اللغة بالمدرسة الرّائدة، وذلك من خلال رصد مجموع الظواهر اللغوية المعتدمة في مقررات اللغة العربية بالسلك الإعدادي، ومن خلال إبراز المراحل الديدكتيكية التي تمرّ منها تلك التعلّمات، وهي: مرحلة الاستشكاف، ثم مرحلة البناء ، ثم مرحلة التوظيف، وأخيرا مرحلة الإدماج في ورشات الكتابة.

النتائج: توصّلت المقالة إلى عدة نتائج أهمها تغيير زاوية النظر في تدريس قواعد اللغة العربية من صفتها المجردة إلى قوتها الإنجازية. ثم إعاة النظر في اختيار القواعد اللغوية التي ينبغي تدريسها واستخلاص المعرفة المدرسية منها. ثم التركيز على جانب قوة الفعل الكلامي باعتباره معيارا لتحقق النجاح.

Title: Military Spending and Developmental Outcomes of the Social Contract in the Middle East

Description: This study examines the impact of military spending on developmental outcomes associated with the social contract in Middle Eastern countries over the period 1995-2023. The Human Development Index (HDI) is used as an indicator of developmental outcomes associated with the social contract. It also serves as a proxy for the state's ability to transform public economic resources into developmental gains in health, education, and standards of living. The study relies on panel data covering 17 countries and employs an econometric framework that combines static models with a dynamic System GMM model to address temporal persistence, endogeneity, and unobserved heterogeneity.

The results indicate a negative and statistically significant effect of military spending on the Human Development Index, an effect that persists after controlling for key macroeconomic factors and after incorporating the dynamic dimension. The findings also reveal a high degree of persistence in HDI, reflecting its cumulative nature over time. Regarding the institutional context, the results do not provide strong evidence of an effective moderating role for the Polity index, as its impact appears limited and statistically weak. Overall, the findings suggest that military spending constitutes a persistent distributive pressure that affects developmental outcomes associated with the social contract within the limits allowed by the data and the adopted methodology.

Title: Overcoming adoption barriers of bio-based material innovation in construction: Exploring hemp-based materials and deriving implications for business models to increase diffusion

Description: The construction industry is increasingly seeking sustainable material alternatives to mitigate its environmental impact. Despite the technological advantages of bio-based materials over conventional materials in construction, their diffusion remains limited. This study focuses on hemp-based materials to understand the barriers preventing their wider use in the construction sector. Through expert interviews, this research identifies key obstacles that hinder adoption and investigates how these can be addressed to achieve higher diffusion. The findings show that professional knowledge constraints dominate in the early adoption stage; customer awareness becomes relevant once technical legitimacy is established, and supply chain limitations and cost considerations become dominant in later stages. Building on these insights, the paper proposes a multi-phase framework aligned with the technology life cycle. The framework illustrates the implications for business models to support the diffusion of bio-based materials in the construction sector.

Keywords: hemp-based materials; bio-based materials; construction; technology adoption; barriers; business models

Title: Using Machine Learning to Identify Brown Dwarfs in Deep JWST Surveys

Description: Deep JWST spectroscopy has revealed a distant population of ultracool dwarf (UCD) stars and brown dwarfs in the Milky Way's thick disk and halo populations. Identifying these rare objects requires efficient, accurate searches of large spectral datasets. We explored machine learning (ML) approaches to isolate UCDs from the overwhelming background of extragalactic sources using JWST/NIRSpec Prism spectroscopic data from the North ecliptic pole EXtragalactic Unified Survey (NEXUS). We evaluated four supervised ML classifiers with variations in model parameters, training sample size and balance, and data pre-conditioning. We find that a maximally-replicated balanced random forest model achieves accuracy, precision, and recall exceeding 99\%. Applied to a single epoch of NEXUS spectroscopy, we identified 25 UCD candidates out of 959 spectra, recovering all 11 visually selected sources, with several remaining false positives being earlier-type stars. This study demonstrates the potential of ML to accelerate UCD discovery in JWST surveys.

Title: Passaporte de Prevenção da Endocardite no Idoso

Description: Com o objetivo de fortalecer a prevenção, a educação em saúde e o acompanhamento contínuo de pacientes com risco de Endocardite Infecciosa ou já com a doença, foi desenvolvido o “ Passaporte de Prevenção da Endocardite no Idoso ”, um livreto educativa destinado ao registro de informações clínicas, fatores de risco, consultas, acompanhamento odontológico e orientações preventivas. O instrumento pode ser utilizado em hospitais, ambulatórios e unidades básicas de saúde, favorecendo a continuidade do cuidado, o monitoramento clínico e a integração entre profissionais, pacientes e familiares. Esse material contém dados de identificação do paciente e/ou avaliação inicial, histórico cardiovascular, fatores de risco para a EI, controle de doenças crônicas (caso as tenha), uso contínuo de medicamentos, consultas médicas e de Enfermagem, acompanhamento odontológico, sinais e sintomas de alerta, orientações preventivas e recomendações para a rede de apoio do paciente. Trata-se de uma forma mais acessível, rápida e eficaz de rastrear a evolução desses casos, além de favorecer o desenvolvimento de um melhor autocuidado e autogestão de saúde ao passo que o próprio paciente tem acesso às suas próprias informações. Também é importante para a continuidade do cuidado para os profissionais que o acompanham.

Title: To Study the Common Etiologies of Pleural Effusion and Their Clinical Profile in Patients Attending in A Tertiary Care Hospital in Delhi

Description: Pleural effusion is an abnormal excess accumulation of fluid in the pleural space. The pleural space is space between the lung and chest wall and normally contains a small amount of fluid about 10 to 20 mL, with a low protein concentration (less than 1.5 g/dL), which serves as a coupling system [1]. Excess fluid accumulation occurs due to disruption of the equilibrium that exists across pleural membranes. Pleural effusion indicates an acute or chronic pathologic process that may be of primary pulmonary origin or of secondary origin related to another organ system.

Pleural effusion is not a diagnosis in itself but it aids in diagnosis of underlying pathological process with evaluation of its cause and further management. Light’s criteria which include serum and pleural fluid biochemical analyses is most commonly used to distinguish between the exudative and transudative pleural effusion (PE) in routine clinical practice [2]. Light’s criteria have high sensitivity for diagnosing exudative pleural effusion but it is also found that occasionally it cannot differentiate the underlying causes such as infections and malignancies. With the advent of various diagnostic aids like pleural fluid cytology, pleural biopsy, ultrasonography, bronchoscopy, thoracoscopy, CT thorax, serological tests like ANA, ADA, Rheumatoid factor, microbiological culture helps the physician to diagnose at an earlier course of the disease. Although most tests have their drawbacks viz thoracoscopy is invasive procedure and leaves 7% of cases undiagnosed; microbiological culture test has high turn-around-time (TAT), CT thorax has high radiation exposure etc. Recently with further advancement, some pleural fluid and serum markers have shown increased specificity and diagnostic accuracy in patients with pleural effusion (PE). For instance, patients with tuberculous PE have high interleukin-27(IL-27), interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), adenosine deaminase (ADA) pleural fluid levels while serum N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) for congestive heart failure (CHF) patients [3]. However, the diagnostic accuracy of other available markers such as tumour markers, procalcitonin (PCT) and C reactive protein (CRP) for malignant and infectious diseases remains unsatisfactory. Therefore, further researches are required to identify novel markers in PE with increased diagnostic accuracy and faster TAT to aid earliest diagnosis and timely management to increase outcome among patients.

Title: Raven: From Scientific Data to Trustworthy Autonomous Discovery

Description: Transformational AI for science will depend less on isolated model capability than on the quality of the scientific data interfaces surrounding each model. Raven is a state-aware agentic architecture for turning heterogeneous data, simulations, literature, and experiments into auditable discovery decisions. Its central design choice is to represent each step as a typed, provenance-carrying state transition and to expose local models and instruments as verifiable capabilities. A materials-discovery testbed demonstrates how domain-specific data, forward-model verification, and reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards can connect scientific data infrastructure to experimentally testable action. Raven: \url{https://ravenllm.com/}

Title: Management of Protected Areas and sustainable use of Caatinga Biodiversity in Brazil

Description: The use of the Brazilian Caatinga biodiversity has not been done in a sustainable way, which
has caused irreversible environmental impacts. The geodiversity of this biome is an important component of the
natural heritage existing here, but it lacks studies that explore mainly the characteristics of the landscape and
its conservation forms. The present work aims to discuss the relevance of the sustainable use of the natural
resources of the Brazilian Caatingas, as well as to present a proposal for conservation of protected landscapes
in Brazil. The present research aims at elaborating and proposing conservation plans for protected landscapes,
essentially those with a high degree of vulnerability, such as the river dunes that accompany the course of the
São Francisco River. The methodology is based essentially on Geosistemic Theory, Ecodynamic Method and
GTP Theory. Therefore, it is crucial to develop conservation measures for protected environments, since the
landscapes are products and records of the geological evolution of the planet and integrate the planet, as well
as corroborate for the sustainable use of the biome. Therefore, it is indispensable to understand the urgency of
the adequate management of protected areas in Brazil, essentially those that safeguard environmental
indicators of paleoeras, paleoclimas and paleoventos.

Title: Cinema, Convivência e Estados de Humor no Envelhecimento: Intervenção Extensionista com Pessoas Idosas no Contexto Universitário

Description: O envelhecimento populacional brasileiro tem se intensificado de forma acelerada e demanda respostas que ultrapassem a abordagem biomédica, incorporando dimensões sociais, culturais, emocionais e relacionais do cuidado. De acordo com o Censo Demográfico de 2022, o Brasil contava com 32.113.490 pessoas com 60 anos ou mais, correspondendo a 15,6% da população total (IBGE, 2023). Esse cenário reforça a necessidade de estratégias institucionais que promovam o envelhecimento saudável, a participação social e a formação de profissionais capazes de reconhecer a pessoa idosa em sua integralidade.

No campo da educação superior, a extensão universitária constitui espaço privilegiado para aproximar universidade e comunidade, articulando ensino, pesquisa e responsabilidade social. A Resolução CNE/CES n. 7/2018 define a extensão como processo interdisciplinar, político-educacional, cultural, científico e tecnológico, capaz de promover interação transformadora entre instituições de ensino superior e sociedade (Brasil, 2018). No curso de Medicina, essa perspectiva dialoga com as Diretrizes Curriculares Nacionais, que orientam a formação de médicos com perfil generalista, humanista, crítico, reflexivo e socialmente responsável (Brasil, 2014).

A experiência relatada insere-se nesse contexto institucional e formativo. No âmbito do Claretiano – Centro Universitário de Rio Claro, o projeto articula-se ao curso de Medicina ao favorecer vivências práticas orientadas pela escuta, pelo vínculo, pela empatia e pela compreensão ampliada do processo de envelhecimento. O próprio perfil divulgado pelo curso de Medicina do Claretiano destaca a formação humana, as metodologias ativas, o pensamento crítico, a responsabilidade profissional e a vivência prática desde o início da graduação como componentes relevantes da trajetória formativa (Claretiano, 2026). Assim, a proposta não se apresenta apenas como uma atividade complementar, mas como uma ação extensionista coerente com o compromisso institucional de formar profissionais sensíveis às necessidades reais da comunidade.

Nesse sentido, a inclusão de pessoas idosas no contexto universitário assume relevância social e pedagógica. Para as pessoas idosas, a universidade torna-se espaço de acolhimento, convivência, expressão de memórias, reconhecimento de trajetórias e fortalecimento de vínculos. Para os estudantes, a presença das pessoas idosas permite contato com histórias de vida, modos diversos de envelhecer e necessidades que nem sempre aparecem nos cenários clínicos tradicionais. A prática contribui, portanto, para deslocar a pessoa idosa da posição de objeto de estudo para a posição de sujeito participante, portador de experiências, saberes e afetos.

A proposta surgiu como desdobramento do estudo de Carmo (2020), no qual foram investigados os efeitos de sessões de mídias cinematográficas nos estados de humor de pessoas idosas. No projeto extensionista aqui relatado, o cinema foi utilizado como dispositivo mediador de convivência e de expressão subjetiva, associado à aplicação da Lista de Estados de Ânimo Reduzida e Ilustrada (LEA-RI) (Volp, 2000), com o intuito de observar possíveis variações nos estados de humor antes e após as sessões audiovisuais. O foco central da experiência foi a intervenção com as pessoas idosas, considerando o cinema como recurso cultural acessível para favorecer bem-estar, interação social e diálogo intergeracional.

Title: Climate memory of CaCO3

Description: caco3_model_and_figures.m: single self-contained MATLAB script (also runs in GNU Octave; no toolboxes required) accompanying Hylen & Sulpis manuscripr on the climate memory of CaCO3. It computes the equilibrium air-sea CO2 exchange per mole of CaCO₃ (ψ_eq) from built-in carbonate chemistry (Lueker K1/K2, Dickson KB, Weiss K0), calibrates a two-mode Earth-system memory kernel against published pulse-response simulations (Archer 2005; Joos et al. 2013; Lord et al. 2016), derives the memory horizons tau_50 and tau_90, evaluates the counterfactual removal efficiency ε = A·ψ(T; x_d) − F·ψ(τ+T; x_p) for the scenarios discussed in the paper, and reproduces Figures 2–4 and Supplementary Figure 1. Sections can be run independently.

Title: Environmental Geochemistry as a Design Basis for Circular Infrastructure in Mexico

Description: This paper is part of an ongoing series on the circular economy by The Cobeal Group. One of the biggest takeaways for the authors was the importance of chemical composition over time. It is standard practice to describe a material at a given point of measurement, but materials continue to change when exposed to water, oxygen, heat, microorganisms, pressure changes, shifts in pH, or simply enough time.

At the same time, the paper cautions against assuming that time itself will neutralize contaminants. Constituents can migrate into water, sediments, soils, or other receiving environments, and in some cases cause lasting harm to living systems. A residual material may contain zinc, arsenic, lead, copper, cadmium, and other elements while those constituents remain capable of being redistributed among mineral phases, dissolved species, precipitates, sorbed surface complexes, and transported material.

Understanding that behavior in a waste-to-value system requires upstream engineering and a working knowledge of geochemistry. In some applications, aerosol science and indoor environmental science may also become relevant because the movement of air, water, and matter is influenced by mechanical systems, physical structures, transport pathways, and surrounding environmental conditions. Their behavior depends on physical state, residence time, reaction conditions, and the environment into which the material is introduced.

A simple taxonomy or laboratory report can tell you what was measured under a defined set of conditions. Deeper chemical analysis can help explain where those elements may reside after years of oxidation, infiltration, drying, heating, biological activity, pH change, or contact with another material.

That is one of the central ideas behind circular engineering: it is not enough to know what a material is today. We also need to understand what it is capable of becoming over time.

Title: Olhar + Verde: como integrar sustentabilidade à sua vida
